summary: Read src/main.rs:1465-1760 (tag parse/cache, run_mmsg_timeout, ensure_tag_poller, TAG_STREAMING, tag_watch_loop), src/main.rs:7370-7558 (wake pipe, 1 s backdrop timer, minute timer), src/main.rs:6026-6072 and 6380-6472 (frame back-pressure/commit/CompositorHandler::frame), src/wallpaper_blur.rs:205-250,440-540 (PANEL_OPEN, park_while_closed, ensure_loaded, probe_loop), src/controlcenter_panel.rs:905-1003,1181-1320 (refresher loop, snapshot readers), src/music_panel.rs:1139-1211, src/tray.rs:152-161, plus the tag parser tests (src/main.rs:8882-8905, src/main.rs:8780-8800). Collapsed idle is genuinely good and cannot be broken by this review: draw_if_ready sets redraw_wanted instead of queueing a second frame while an ack is outstanding, CompositorHandler::frame clears frame_pending and honours redraw_wanted, so a still island commits zero buffers; the 33/s dictation-bar packets and the ~3-line-per-switch mmsg bursts collapse into one redraw via the tag wake pipe, which drains its 64-byte buffer and only draws when active_tag_cached() != last_tag_drawn; wallpaper_blur::ensure_loaded is (mtime,len)-gated and ensure_probe_running is a Once; all timers are one-shot chains (16 ms morph, 33 ms lock, minute) that stop when idle; measured collapsed cost 0.5% CPU / 60.5 MB RSS and Pss tail +0.0 / peak +1.3 MB agree. What does NOT hold up is the OPEN state and the freshness contract: the r2 #5b gate made the closed state cheap but left the ControlCenter refresher spinning with no sleep at all while the panel is open (measured here: an 11-call nmcli/bluetoothctl/brightnessctl/wpctl/swaync/pgrep snapshot costs 0.12 s CPU per pass on this box, and the loop issues it back-to-back), the 60 s backdrop probe removed the 1 s freshness without adding the eager wake its own comment claims (so a tag switch or wallpaper change leaves the panel/morph frost stale for up to a minute plus the entire open duration), and the tag stream's fallback is gated on a flag set before the first line arrives with no silence watchdog, on a child that is never reaped on panel exit. No unprofiled guesswork is scored as a defect: morph pacing and absolute presentation latency are outside this lens and remain unresolved in /tmp/r3-measure.json, so this verdict says nothing new about them.

findings.title: ControlCenter refresher has no sleep while the panel is open — subprocess spin at ~10-25x the intended rate
findings.detail: park_while_closed (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:233-245) returns true IMMEDIATELY when a panel is open, without sleeping; it is a parking helper, so every caller must sleep itself. music_panel does (src/music_panel.rs:1207 trailing std::thread::sleep(1 s)), ControlCenter does not: src/controlcenter_panel.rs:983-990 is `if !panel_open { park(5s); if !panel_open { continue } } refresh_cc_cache(); park(5s);` — with the panel open the first branch is skipped and the trailing park returns instantly, so refresh_cc_cache() runs in a tight loop instead of once per CC_REFRESH_INTERVAL (src/controlcenter_panel.rs:910). read_live_snapshot (src/controlcenter_panel.rs:930-968) forks nmcli -t dev wifi, bluetoothctl show, nmcli radio, swaync-client -D, brightnessctl g + m, wpctl get-volume, pgrep -x wlsunset, swaync-client -c (+ bluetoothctl/pactl while a submenu is open). Measured locally, that 11-call snapshot set costs 0.12 s CPU per pass (5 passes: 0.313 u + 0.285 s = 0.598 s CPU / 0.687 s wall), and the loop then re-issues it immediately, i.e. ~8-10 passes/s ≈ near a full core plus a fork storm of ~90-100 short-lived processes per second, versus the intended 0.2 passes/s. That runs during the exact interaction the owner judges on smoothness: the CC morph is a 16 ms frame chain (src/main.rs:5789) competing with that fork storm, and the SoC/battery cost is the one the r2 comment at src/controlcenter_panel.rs:978-982 claims to have fixed. Profile it to confirm the magnitude (top -H during an open CC, or sum /proc/<child>/stat on the refresher thread), but the loop structure alone is unambiguous. Fix: mirror music_panel — make the trailing call a real sleep, e.g. `std::thread::sleep(CC_REFRESH_INTERVAL)` after refresh_cc_cache(), or change park_while_closed to return early-but-still-nap (return true after sleeping one SLICE) so no caller can spin; add a debug counter assert that refresh passes/s <= 2 while open.

findings.title: Live-backdrop clean frame is up to 60 s stale (plus the whole open duration) and the comment claiming eager refresh describes a path that does not exist
findings.detail: probe_loop (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:498-539) now sleeps 60_000 ms unconditionally, and while PANEL_OPEN it only runs probe_backdrop() strips (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:502-511), so the clean frame in LIVE_CACHE is captured at most once a minute and never while any menu is open. The comment at src/wallpaper_blur.rs:529-537 justifies that with 'reload and tag changes refresh eagerly through the other paths' — there is no such path: the only entry points are live_backdrop() (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:250) read at src/main.rs:2709, src/main.rs:4164 and src/launcher_panel.rs:1180, and ensure_probe_running() from ensure_loaded (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:452), which is a Once and only starts the thread. Nothing marks the cache dirty and live_backdrop_age_secs() (src/wallpaper_blur.rs:256) has zero callers. Consequences: switch tag or change wallpaper, open a panel, and the frost behind every panel and behind the menu-endpoint morph capsule is sampled from a frame up to 60 s old (and stays that way for the entire time the panel is open, since captures are suppressed while open); the collapsed pill's frost can equally lag a tag switch by up to a minute. This is the 'incorrect frost at open' class of visual defect the owner's replica is judged on, and it is cheap to fix: on a tag/state change or ensure_loaded reload, set a STALE flag (or store a generation counter) that makes probe_loop break its 60 s sleep early and take one full capture the next time PANEL_OPEN is false, and use live_backdrop_age_secs() in the draw path to mark the frame stale instead of leaving it as dead code.

findings.title: Tag stream declares itself healthy before its first line and has no silence watchdog; the watcher is never reaped on panel exit
findings.detail: tag_watch_loop stores TAG_STREAMING=true at src/main.rs:1724, immediately after spawn and before any line is parsed, and clears it only when reader.lines() returns (src/main.rs:1726-1734) — there is no timeout on that read and no staleness check. The fallback poller is gated on exactly that flag (src/main.rs:1656), so if `mmsg watch all-tags` stays alive but silent (mango restart, socket half-close without EOF, a partially consumed stdout) the highlight freezes with no fallback and no log line. Fix: stamp AN_INSTANT at each parsed line and only treat the stream as authoritative while the stamp is younger than ~5 s, otherwise let the poller run (and/or wrap the reader in a thread with a recv_timeout, as run_mmsg_timeout already does). Separately, the SIGTERM path (src/main.rs:7741-7757) only calls loop_signal.stop(); the Child lives inside tag_watch_loop (src/main.rs:1714-1735) with no shared handle, no pre_exec PDEATHSIG and no Drop kill, so every panel restart orphans a `mmsg` — confirmed live: pid 15580 `mmsg watch all-tags`, PPID 15556 (the running panel), RSS 6332 kB, elapsed equal to the panel's own. Cheap fix: keep the child pid in a static and kill it in the signal handler / on loop exit, or set PDEATHSIG(SIGTERM) via CommandExt::pre_exec.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Close the two open-state holes and the freshness contract, then re-measure the open state the way the collapsed state was measured: (1) no refresher or probe thread may busy-loop when a panel is open — park_while_closed must nap at least one slice before returning true (so ControlCenter stops at ~2 passes/s, verified by a passes-per-second assertion or a top -H sample during an open CC), and the same audit applied to every park_while_closed caller; (2) a tag switch, a state change or a wallpaper reload must invalidate and eagerly re-capture the live-backdrop clean frame at the next closed moment, with live_backdrop_age_secs() consumed by the draw path so a stale frost is impossible to ship silently; (3) the tag stream's health must be time-based rather than 'child is alive' — a silent stream must fall back to the poll within a few seconds, and the child must be reaped on shutdown (PDEATHSIG or a stored pid) so restarts do not accumulate mmsg processes; (4) publish the open-state numbers (CPU/RSS with a menu open, and the wake latency from tag switch to committed frame) next to the collapsed 0.5%/60.5 MB figures, so 'idle' and 'wake' are both evidenced rather than only idle; and (5) state plainly, in the brief, that this lens does not certify presentation smoothness — the measured motion failure (poses 11/14/13 vs ~14, worst settle 277.3 ms, p50 21.7 ms being send-to-accepted rather than on-screen) still has to be closed by the motion lens. With those in place the panel would read as cheap and instant in both states, which is what 9+ under this lens requires.
